chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Haytham, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the juice (of grapes or similar fruit) that is cooked over fire until it boils from the time it is drawn; its owner drinks it. He said: 'When it changes from its state and boils, there is no good in it until two-thirds of it disappears and one-third remains.'

key_terms.اَلْعَصِير: Fruit juice, specifically grape juice in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for permissible consumption of boiled fruit juice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the preparation of *asir* (fruit juice), establishing a specific criterion for its permissibility based on the extent of reduction. The hadith indicates that if the juice boils and alters its state, it remains impermissible or less desirable until two-thirds evaporates, leaving one-third, a rule often linked to the concept of *istihlak* (consumption of the original substance's properties) or ensuring the removal of impurities. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical transformation of foodstuffs to determine their ritual purity and quality.
